title: Rate limiter
context: Implement a token-bucket rate limiter for the public API: one bucket per API key, a burst up to capacity, then a steady refill rate. It is called from many request threads at once. The doc comment has the exact rules.

points.title: One bucket per key in a concurrent map
points.why: Buckets are created on first use from many threads, so the map must be safe to update concurrently.

points.title: Refill lazily from elapsed time
points.why: No background timer is needed: on each call, add elapsed seconds × rate, then cap at capacity.
points.fix: Store tokens and the last update time per bucket; refill on every tryAcquire.

points.title: Atomic check-and-take per bucket
points.why: Refilling, checking and taking a token must happen as one step, or two threads can both take the last token.
points.fix: Synchronize on the bucket (not the whole limiter), or use a lock or CAS loop per bucket.

points.title: Tokens capped at capacity
points.why: Without the cap, a key that was idle for an hour could send an unlimited burst.

points.title: Buckets for old keys are never removed
points.why: With millions of keys the map grows forever. Fine for an interview, but worth mentioning.
points.fix: Evict idle buckets (a Caffeine cache with expireAfterAccess), or keep buckets in Redis with a TTL.
